question.leadin: This man arrested the "Gang of Eight" which led a coup in August 1991 to remove him from power.
question.text: Name this Soviet president who was the eighth and final leader of the USSR before its downfall.
question.clue: This leader, who described his diplomacy with the "Sinatra Doctrine," appointed Eduard Shevardnadze as his Minister of Foreign Affairs and succeeded Constantin Chernenko.

swap.text: This city that sits on both sides of the Dnieper ("duh-NEE-per") River is home to the St. Sophia Cathedral and the historic Golden Gate. It is the capital of the Ukraine.
swap.clue: It's not Novgorod, but a grand prince of this city was named Yaroslav the Wise.

question.leadin: In the late 17th century, this ruler went on a Grand Embassy of Europe, exploring methods to Westernize his country.
question.text: Name this "Great" member of the Romanov dynasty.
question.clue: This ruler disguised himself as "Mikhailov" and studied shipbuilding in the Netherlands during his Grand Embassy.

swap.text: Peter's reforms of Russia included decreasing the power of the boyars by establishing this system with fourteen levels of military, judicial, and civil service titles.
swap.clue: Catherine the Great provided an automatic seven-year promotion clause within this system, which created a merit-based bureaucracy of civil service starting in 1722.

question.leadin: The pirate Stenka Razin, who led a 1670 uprising against Moscow, was of this ethnic group.
question.text: Name these militaristic people of Southern Russia. An unsuccessful 1773 to 1775 rebellion of these people was led by the deluded Yemelyan Pugachev.
question.clue: A series of military campaigns in Poland called the "Deluge" occurred following an uprising of these people led by Bogdan Khmelnytsky ("k'mel-NIT-skee").

swap.leadin: Upon learning of Islam's prohibitions on alcohol, a ruler of this polity exclaimed "drinking is the joy" of his people, and converted to Christianity instead.
swap.text: Name this polity, whose history is reported in Nestor's Primary Chronicle. One ruler of this polity, Vladimir the Great, ordered the mass baptism of its citizens in the Dnieper ("Knee-per") River during its Christianization.
swap.clue: Its leaders used a system of succession in which the throne would pass to the eldest brother of the deceased, called the rota or "ladder" system.

question.leadin: A huge cannon known as the Raevsky Redoubt formed a crucial part of the defender's line in this battle.
question.text: Mikhail Kutuzov led the Russian defense in this 1812 battle where Matvei Platov led a cossack charge against Eugene de Beauharnais. This battle was the single bloodiest day of the Napoleonic Wars.
question.clue: Pierre Bezhukov spends most of this battle in a battery at the Raevsky Redoubt, and Mikhael Kutusov is described as being inactive during it.

swap.leadin: Identify some conflicts in the Caucasus.
swap.text: This Russian republic with capital Grozny saw the defeat of an overwhelmingly superior Russian force by the Republic of Ichkeria in the early 1990s.
swap.clue: On Knowledge Day, terrorists from this polity occupied a school in neighboring Beslan.

question.leadin: This man's brother Svyatopolk the Accursed killed three of his other brothers before coming to power.
question.text: Identify this eleventh-century Slavic ruler who built the Golden Gate and Cathedral of St. Sophia. His law code earned him the epithet "the Wise."
question.clue: He took Kiev from his half-brother Sviatoslav the Accursed.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about a noted political leader.
swap.text: Assassinated outside of Mexico City in 1940, this leader of the Revolution split with Stalin after Lenin's death and was eventually expelled from the politburo.
swap.clue: This man advocated a policy of "permanent revolution" as opposed to a rival's theory of "socialism in one country."

question.leadin: Name these places in where news has occurred over the past few years.
question.text: International Chess Federation president Kirsan Ilyumzhinov has run this constituent as a personal dictatorship since 1995, funneling tax dollars into extravagant monuments to chess and having opposition journalists murdered.

swap.leadin: The engineer John Fox Burgoyne offered key recommendations during this event.
swap.text: Name this siege carried out for almost a year against Russian defenses at a strategically located city. The battles of Balaklava and Inkerman were part of this siege which ended shortly after the Malakoff redoubt fell.
swap.clue: The Battle of Balaclava, at which the Charge of the Light Brigade took place, was part of the siege of this city.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the Battle of Manzikert.
question.text: The fourth Byzantine emperor of this name was captured at Manzikert.
question.clue: Anna Anderson claimed to be a lost member of this house.

swap.leadin: Nationalist historians who follow the invalidated Litvinist school credit this modern country's people with founding the Grand Duchy of Lithuania and dub the 16th century its "golden age."
swap.text: Name this country divided by the medieval Principalities of Turov and Polotsk. A rushnyk folk pattern appears on the red, white, and green flag of this country, which historically included Black and White Ruthenia.
swap.answerHtml: Belarus [or Republic of Belarus or Riespublika Bielaruś or Respublika Bielaruś; accept Byelorussia] (The name “Belarus” means “White Rus’.”)
swap.clue: Flowing through the center of the country is the Berezina River, while the Daugava River cuts through the very north.

question.text: Brusilov also led the failed 1917 June Offensive planned by this leader of the Provisional Government, who was targeted in the Kornilov Affair. This man issued Order No. 8 and fled after the October Revolution.
question.clue: This head of the Russian provisional government of 1917 who was deposed by the Bolsheviks.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the man who was king of Poland until 1831.
swap.text: The Russians attempted to relieve Sevastopol in this November 1854 battle, the last major Crimean War conflict before Nicholas's death, but the Sandbag Battery and some fog let the outnumbered British win.
swap.clue: One general in this split his column of forces and passed one portion to FF von Mueller.

question.leadin: This figure retired to the New Jerusalem Monastery after opposing Tsar Alexis's 1649 law code, which allowed monastery lands to be taxed.
question.text: Name this figure, whose introduction of rites such as signing the cross with three fingers angered Old Believers like Avvakum, leading to a schism known as the Raskol.

swap.leadin: This namesake of a class of icebreaker ships is attested in the charter of Kostroma, which was partially given to his son-in-law Bogdan in tribute to this man's deeds.
swap.text: Name this legendary figure, who is said to have led a Polish army looking for the Hypatian Monastery into death in the deep woods instead.

question.text: In this revolution, demonstrators forced the resignation of Eduard Shevardnadze, and Mikhail Saakashvili won the election that followed to become the president of Georgia.
question.clue: James Baker attempted to prevent this event by developing an electoral formula, which was subsequently ignored.

swap.leadin: This man organized the withdrawal of Soviet troops from Afghanistan, and he was instrumental in negotiating START.
swap.text: Name this man who succeeded Andrei Gromyko as Soviet Foreign Minister.
swap.clue: The Adjara crisis was sparked by this leader's overthrow, in which demonstrators led by Mikheil Saakashvili stormed their nation's Parliament, carrying a certain flower.
